Design a bold text poster with layered depth

Use short text, controlled extrusion and readable color contrast to make a useful PNG or SVG poster.

By NepocorePublished & updated 28 October 20263 min read
In this guide
  1. Let one short phrase lead
  2. Control three color roles
  3. Use depth as emphasis
  4. Choose the right export and accompanying text
← All guides

Let one short phrase lead

A text poster works best when the reader recognizes its message before noticing the effect. Start with one short word or phrase, such as MAKE IT, OPEN DAY or KEEP GOING. The text maker supports up to 24 characters, but a shorter line gives each letter more space. Long text automatically needs smaller letters.

Choose a type style that fits the purpose. A simple sans serif can make a bold event label, while a serif changes the mood. Do not depend on a decorative effect to make an unclear message interesting. Write the final wording first, then adjust the visual treatment.

Control three color roles

The front color carries the message, the depth color creates the extrusion, and the background separates the whole word from the page. Start with a dark depth color and a light front face, or reverse that relationship. Check whether the front letters remain recognizable where the layers overlap.

For example, try cream letters, deep green depth and a pale green background. If the message becomes difficult to read when viewed small, increase separation between the front face and the background before adding more layers. The contrast checker can inform color choices, but it does not evaluate the complete decorative shape automatically.

Use depth as emphasis

The effect is built from offset copies of vector text. More layers make a deeper extrusion and can also crowd letter interiors. This is an illustration of depth on a flat page, rather than a 3D model with lighting, geometry or a rotating camera.

Compare a shallow version with a deeper one. Check enclosed areas in A, B, O and R, plus the gap between neighboring letters. An effect that merges those shapes may reduce readability. Leave enough blank space around the word for the poster to breathe.

  1. Enter the final short phrase.
  2. Choose the letter style and three colors.
  3. Start with a modest layer count and create a preview.
  4. Inspect the message at thumbnail size.
  5. Export PNG for predictable pixels or SVG for further vector editing.

Choose the right export and accompanying text

PNG captures the rendered appearance on your device. SVG retains editable text and vector shapes, but another computer may substitute a font and change the appearance. If consistent lettering matters, inspect the SVG on the destination system or use the PNG at sufficient dimensions.

When using the poster on a web page, include the important wording as ordinary text or meaningful alternative text. A raster headline should not be the only accessible version of an event name, date or instruction. Keep the source wording and chosen settings in your project notes so a later revision does not require guessing. For print, confirm the physical size and resolution separately rather than assuming that an SVG or PNG filename guarantees a print-ready document.
